title: 5G coverage expanded in CAMANAVA for TNT

blocks.text: TNT is bringing its 5G experience closer to more communities, now covering Caloocan, Malabon, Navotas, and Valenzuela, collectively known as CAMANAVA. It is also expanding its 5G coverage across the country.

With significantly faster, more responsive connectivity, students can access online learning resources, riders can manage bookings, and small businesses can communicate with customers and process orders more efficiently.

“We want to make 5G more accessible and meaningful to Filipinos by showing how reliable connectivity can support their everyday needs – from staying on top of schoolwork and managing livelihood activities to finding new opportunities to earn and grow. Through our rollout in CAMANAVA, we hope to bring these benefits closer to more communities,” said Lloyd R. Manaloto, FVP and officer-in-charge of Smart.

Powered by 5G, subscribers can also now access AI.Smart, a one-stop digital workspace that brings together multiple AI tools, including AWS Nova, ChatGPT, Claude, Google Gemini, and Thinking Machines through a single web-based interface, helping them explore new ideas, support learning, and take on everyday tasks.
Getting started with 5G

TNT SIMs currently available in the market are 5G-ready, so subscribers do not need to replace their SIM just to access 5G. They need a 5G-capable smartphone, 5G enabled in their phone settings, and access to an area with 5G coverage.

On Android devices, users can generally find the 5G option under Settings, then Connections or Mobile Networks, depending on the model. On compatible iPhones, they can go to Settings, Cellular, Cellular Data Options, then Voice & Data.
Putting 5G connectivity to work
For 21-year-old Jomari Ian Yambao of Navotas, balancing college and multiple side gigs is part of working toward a better future.

A student taking up Marketing Management at Navotas Polytechnic College, Ian is one of the primary breadwinners for his family of six. After school, he takes motorcycle taxi bookings and helps coordinate seafood deliveries, making the most of available opportunities to earn while pursuing his education.

Staying connected is essential to managing these responsibilities. Ian relies on TNT 5G connection to check school announcements, attend online classes, manage motorcycle taxi bookings, and coordinate seafood deliveries.

He has been doing these side gigs to support himself since 2019, after his family’s financial problems left him with little support. Despite the demands of school and work, he remains focused on his ambition to launch a business of his own.
On a good day, he earns around P600 to P1,000 from motorcycle taxi work and P1,000 from seafood-related work, helping him contribute to household expenses and cover his daily needs.

His connection also comes in handy when classmates need internet access for schoolwork. By sharing his mobile hotspot, he sometimes earns an additional P150 to P200, helping cover his data expenses, meals, and transportation.
For Ian, every opportunity counts as he works toward completing his education and helping his family.
Reaching more communities
Ian’s experience reflects how mobile connectivity can support Filipinos’ everyday needs—not just for entertainment, but also for education, work, and livelihood.
By expanding its 5G reach, TNT aims to help more Filipinos make practical use of connectivity for education, work, and everyday activities.

For students like Ian, staying connected helps make it easier to manage competing responsibilities while working toward a better future. As TNT brings 5G to more communities, it hopes to help more Filipinos pursue the goals that matter to them.
To know more about TNT and how to access its 5G network, visit https://tntph.com/Pages/signal.
